title: Nested Function Calls
concept: You can use the result of one function call directly as the argument to another — this is called nesting or composition.
why: Nesting eliminates temporary variables and expresses multi-step transformations concisely.
syntax_ref:
outer_function(inner_function(args))
// inner runs first, result feeds into outer
tips: Inner function calls run FIRST, then outer — read from inside out
Nesting works because functions return values that match parameter types
Don't nest more than 2-3 levels deep — it becomes hard to read
Nesting and composition mean the same thing in programming
common_mistakes: Getting the order wrong: `f(g(x))` calls g first, then f
Nesting functions that don't return values (Unit functions)
Type mismatch: inner function returns Int but outer expects Str
